Analysis: Hypothesis 2 offers greater novelty by integrating the role of noncoding RNAs as an additional regulatory layer alongside FTO-mediated m6A demethylation. It establishes a link between metabolic stress and FTO upregulation and outlines a more detailed experimental strategy (m6A-RIP sequencing, RNA stability assays) to pinpoint direct targets in lipid metabolism. This integrative approach, despite necessitating further mechanistic detail, appears more comprehensive and testable while maintaining plausible safety. In comparison, Hypothesis 1, although strong and innovative in its own right with spatial and single-cell transcriptomic methods, remains somewhat narrower by focusing primarily on inflammatory and metabolic transcripts. Therefore, the additional mechanistic depth and broader experimental framework of Hypothesis 2 make it the superior proposal.
